clearedSpotChecks.check: Lead L-1109: does Nitro rc.9 b72783f give the specified word on the targeted set, the battery and script set 1 when the answer comes from the linux-amd64 backend of Robinhood Chain.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The raw files hold what the item says: l1109-targeted.json has 143 batches, 0 mismatches, 0 errors, 143 with an amd64 bracket and 127 with an amd64-amd64 bracketed send; l1109-battery.json 167 batches, 0 mismatches, 141 amd64-amd64; l1109-pmdiff.json and l1109-pmdiff-b.json 250 scripts each, 0 mismatches, PoolManager code sha256 a7aaa3ba equal to cycle 25. arch_runs.py lines 50-69 compare every returned word against battery.expected and check the answer length, and lines 85-99 compare each script hash with the cycle 25 reference hashes, so a short or empty answer counts as a failure. I reran 4 targeted batches (starts 27000, 30600, 58200, 61800) 3 times each against https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com with web3_clientVersion before and after: 12 answers of 600 words, 0 mismatches, 6 sends with linux-amd64 on both sides and 4 with linux-arm64 on both sides. The per-request routing claim holds in my own brackets, which also showed mixed pairs. The test covers only the read path of the answering node, which the item itself notes.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Does any of the three nodes route an address to native precompile code that the earlier precompile sweeps (0x01 to 0x1ff, 0x64 to 0x74, 0xc8, 0xff, 0xa4b05) did not call from the PoolManager address.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I called eth_config on https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc, https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com and https://rpc.elysium.kinetiq.xyz. Each returned 36 precompiles: 0x01 to 0x11, 0x64 to 0x69, 0x6b to 0x74, 0xff, 0x100 and 0xa4b05, systemContracts HISTORY_STORAGE_ADDRESS 0x0000f90827f1c53a10cb7a02335b175320002935, and no next fork entry. Every address lies inside the swept ranges. eth_config reports the node's configured precompile set; it cannot show code paths that ArbOS runs for ordinary addresses (Stylus programs are user deployed and are outside this check), so the item clears only the native precompile routing question.

clearedSpotChecks.check: ArbOS state that changes what the PoolManager's native and token paths meet: scheduled upgrade, native token management, transaction filtering, calldata price flag, chain owners and ArbOS version, read at the head on 2026-11-26.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I reran the reads myself. ArbOwnerPublic 0x6b at the head (Arbitrum One block 527,805,073, Robinhood Chain 123,694,050, Elysium 11,169,404): getScheduledUpgrade() returns two zero words on all three, getNativeTokenManagementFrom() 0 on all three, getTransactionFilteringFrom() 0x6a3baaa0 (1,782,295,200) on Robinhood Chain and 0 elsewhere, isCalldataPriceIncreaseEnabled() 0 on all three. ArbSys 0x64 arbOSVersion() returns 0x74 (116) on all three. I did not reread getAllChainOwners(); the stored answer in raw/arbos_state.txt shows three, two and one owners. Holders of chain owner keys are governance actors in any case.
